top_story.headline: Rep. Jamie Raskin bill would put a Trump-era 'authoritarianism' exhibit in the Smithsonian
top_story.dek: Both chambers held only brief pro forma sessions Tuesday, so the day's news is in the bills introduced.
paragraphs: On a day with no votes, Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD-8) introduced a bill directing the Smithsonian Institution to collect, preserve and permanently display, in the National Museum of American History, artifacts reflecting "the rise of governmental propaganda, corruption, and authoritarianism" during President Donald J. Trump's two terms. The bill text defines those terms as January 20, 2017 to January 20, 2021 and January 20, 2025 to January 20, 2029.

It was referred to the Committee on House Administration and, additionally, the Committee on Natural Resources. The House met for two minutes and held no votes, so nothing beyond introduction occurred.

sections.headline: Pro forma sessions in both chambers; 22 House measures introduced
paragraphs: The Senate met at 1:31 p.m. on Tuesday, October 6, 2026, in a pro forma session lasting about half a minute and adjourned until 1:30 p.m. on Friday, October 9. The House met at 4 p.m. and adjourned at 4:02 p.m.; the Congressional Record's Daily Digest reports no roll call votes and no quorum calls.

Members introduced 17 House bills (H.R. 10751–10767), one concurrent resolution and four simple resolutions. Most are narrow, but three drew attention: Rep. Josh Gottheimer's (D-NJ-5) bill limiting United States contributions to the United Nations, his resolution on the October 7 anniversary, and Rep. Jamie Raskin's Smithsonian bill. The Daily Digest also lists two committee reports filed on veterans bills, H.R. 6698 and H.R. 7260.

items: H.R. 10751, sponsored by Rep. Jack Bergman (R-MI-1) — would remove restrictions on dental therapist services under the Community Health Aide Program in the Indian Health Care Improvement Act. Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources and the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10752, sponsored by Rep. Troy A. Carter (D-LA-2) — would create a task force on artificial intelligence inside the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Referred to the Committee on Homeland Security.

H.R. 10753, sponsored by Rep. Elijah Crane (R-AZ-2) — the Tribal Veterans Voucher Flexibility Act, would let tribes voluntarily reallocate vouchers under the Tribal HUD-VASH veterans housing program. Referred to the Committee on Financial Services.

H.R. 10754, sponsored by Rep. Elijah Crane (R-AZ-2) — the Rural Disaster Fairness Act of 2026, would update the indicators of a disaster's local impact in the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2018. Referred to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

H.R. 10755, sponsored by Rep. Jasmine Crockett (D-TX-30) — would name the post office at 475 East FM 1382 in Cedar Hill, Texas, the "Eugene Gates Jr. Post Office Building." Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
H.R. 10756, sponsored by Rep. Mike Ezell (R-MS-4) — would reauthorize Regional Ocean Partnerships. Referred to the Committee on Natural Resources.
H.R. 10757, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — would limit United States contributions to the United Nations. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.R. 10758, sponsored by Rep. Jeff Hurd (R-CO-3) — would have the Secretary of Veterans Affairs award grants to state entities to expand structured outdoor recreation programs for veterans. Referred to the Committee on Veterans' Affairs.

H.R. 10759, sponsored by Rep. John James (R-MI-10) — would set up a tariff-funded program to shield United States manufacturers, workers, farmers and supply chains from economic harm caused by tariffs and foreign retaliation, and to encourage reshoring. Referred to the Committee on Financial Services and the Committee on Ways and Means.

H.R. 10760, sponsored by Rep. Thomas H. Kean (R-NJ-7) — the Healthy Minds for a Better Future Act, would create a multiagency Middle School Mental Health Task Force at the Department of Education and the Department of Health and Human Services. Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10761, sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-CA-17) — the Campus Accountability and Safety Act of 2026, would amend the Jeanne Clery Campus Safety Act to combat campus sexual assault. Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce and the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10762, sponsored by Rep. Michael Lawler (R-NY-17) — the Anthony Amoros Law Right to Know Act, would require used-car sellers to keep a vehicle's airbag system working or clearly disclose when one is missing or disabled. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce and the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10763, sponsored by Rep. Julia Letlow (R-LA-5) — the Know Your Risk Act, would direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to report to Congress on breast cancer risk assessment tools. Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.R. 10764, sponsored by Rep. Gwen Moore (D-WI-4) — the Executive Settlement Review Act, would require set procedures for compromise settlements or awards involving executive branch officials. Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

H.R. 10765, sponsored by Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD-8) — would direct the Smithsonian Institution to collect and permanently display, in the National Museum of American History, artifacts reflecting the rise of governmental propaganda, corruption and authoritarianism during President Donald J. Trump's two terms. Referred to the Committee on House Administration and the Committee on Natural Resources.

H.R. 10766, sponsored by Rep. Keith Self (R-TX-3) — would require the Department of Defense to add assets critical to the Golden Dome missile defense system to its Critical Asset List. Referred to the Committee on Armed Services.

H.R. 10767, sponsored by Rep. Adrian Smith (R-NE-3) — the Fair Play Enforcement Act, would impose an excise tax on colleges and universities that allow specified individuals to take part in intercollegiate athletics. Referred to the Committee on Ways and Means.

H. Con. Res. 123, sponsored by Rep. Teresa Leger Fernandez (D-NM-3) — would recognize the disparity in wages paid to Latinas and its effect on women, families and the economy. Referred to the Committee on Education and Workforce.
H.Res. 1617, sponsored by Rep. Earl L. "Buddy" Carter (R-GA-1) — would recognize October as "American Pharmacy Month." Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce.

H.Res. 1618, sponsored by Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-5) — would mark the third anniversary of the October 7, 2023, attacks on Israel, honor the victims and hostages, and call for the complete disarmament of Hamas. It has dozens of cosponsors from both parties. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.Res. 1619, sponsored by Rep. Glenn Thompson (R-PA-15) — would reaffirm German-American friendship and support continued cooperation between the two countries. Referred to the Committee on Foreign Affairs.

H.Res. 1620, sponsored by Rep. Nikema Williams (D-GA-5) — would support the goals of "National Nonviolence Week" to raise awareness of youth violence. Referred to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
